name: Asaph
overview: Asaph was a male Levite known primarily as a singer, serving in the worship of God according to the biblical record. He is identified as the father of Zichri, emphasizing his role within the Levitical lineage. His contributions to the worship life of Israel highlight the importance of music and praise in the service of the Lord.
namesAndTitles: The name Asaph means 'gatherer' and is a proper name found in Scripture. This meaning may reflect his role in gathering people or contributions for worship, but the text simply records the name without indicating it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Asaph was a descendant of Levi and the father of Zichri. These relationships place him firmly within the Levitical family, entrusted with duties related to temple worship and music.
scriptureSignificance: Asaph's significance lies in his role as a Levite singer, contributing to the spiritual life of Israel through music and worship. Being the father of Zichri connects him to the ongoing Levitical service, affirming the hereditary nature of temple duties. His presence in the biblical narrative underscores the vital role of worship leaders in guiding God's people in praise.
